- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 10–30% for 30d horizon.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.33) or volatile, model often underestimates or spikes too early; add a 5–15% downward bias to avoid overcorrection.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 3x recent mean), model frequently overcorrects; apply a “cool-down” rule: reduce forecast by 20–40% for next 3–5 days.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model tends to lag; adjust forecast to align with sentiment’s recent direction (e.g., if sentiment shifts to bearish, reduce forecast 10–20%).
- For 30d horizon, model often fails to capture mean reversion; if recent 18-day average is >2.0, forecast should not exceed 1.8 unless sentiment strongly bullish.
- If sentiment is neutral (0.33–0.67) and price is trending, model often misses the turn; apply a “sentiment-weighted smoothing” rule: average sentiment with 3-day moving average to adjust forecast.
